expansion_contract.fact_row: verified official consumer-rights, service-quality, contractual or workflow fact
expansion_contract.boundary_row: prevents tariff eligibility, compensation events, complaints, prices or switching processes from being promoted to exact postcode or parcel coverage without accepted r2 bytes and hardened postjoin evidence

source_routes.name: Ofcom One Touch Switch enforcement close

facts.detail: Social tariffs are lower-price broadband or phone packages for people receiving Universal Credit, Pension Credit and certain other benefits.
Ofcom states that the person receiving the qualifying benefit needs to be the main person on the contract.

guard_streams.write_limit: Benefit eligibility does not prove that a specific address is serviceable.

facts.detail: Ofcom's 22 June 2026 page states that current social-tariff prices range from £10 to £24.
Ofcom states that most listed social tariffs offer superfast broadband above 30 Mbit/s.

guard_streams.write_limit: Advertised package speed is not measured parcel throughput or exact address availability.

facts.detail: Where the current provider offers a social tariff, an eligible customer can switch to it at any time without a switching charge.
Ofcom says social-tariff prices do not rise mid-contract and customers do not pay an early-leaving fee.

guard_streams.write_limit: Commercial protections cannot be used as evidence of network coverage.

facts.detail: Ofcom warns that providers may not cover every premises in the regions shown in its social-tariff table.
Address coverage should be checked with the provider or Ofcom coverage checker.

guard_streams.write_limit: A regional tariff listing must not promote any parcel without exact current service evidence.

facts.detail: Delayed-repair compensation applies when a reported loss of service is not fully fixed after two full working days.
From 1 April 2026 the delayed-repair amount is £10.34 per calendar day.

guard_streams.write_limit: Compensation eligibility is incident evidence, not broadband availability or speed evidence.

facts.detail: A missed engineer appointment, or cancellation with less than 24 hours' notice, attracts £32.31.
A delayed start of a promised new service attracts £6.46 per calendar day.

guard_streams.write_limit: A planned appointment or start date does not prove successful installation.

facts.detail: Unless otherwise agreed, compensation should be credited no later than 30 calendar days after the qualifying event is resolved or occurs.
A provider may offer another form of compensation of equal or higher value if it discloses the bill-credit value.

guard_streams.write_limit: Payment handling must remain separate from technical coverage records.

facts.detail: The scheme covers residential fixed broadband and landline products supplied by participating providers.
Home equipment or activity, contract breach, customer-caused failure or customer-delayed repair can exclude automatic compensation.

guard_streams.write_limit: Scheme scope cannot be generalized to every provider, business line or parcel.

facts.detail: Residential customers, qualifying small businesses and qualifying not-for-profits can use independent ADR free of charge for unresolved disputes.
ADR access is available after six weeks from the initial complaint or earlier with a deadlock letter, subject to the stated time limits.

guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint escalation status is not proof of a network fault at another parcel.

facts.detail: Providers must maintain an accessible complaints code with phone, postal and email or webform contact routes.
Providers must explain investigation steps and timeframes, take prompt active steps, and tell the customer the outcome.

guard_streams.write_limit: A complaint-handling process cannot establish coverage, orderability or speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom approves CISAS and Communications Ombudsman as the two ADR schemes.
Customers must use the ADR scheme to which their provider belongs.

guard_streams.write_limit: ADR membership is provider-level administrative evidence only.

facts.detail: Since January 2025 new contracts cannot set main monthly price rises by inflation or percentages.
Any specified increase must be shown prominently in pounds and pence, with timing, before signup.

guard_streams.write_limit: Price transparency does not demonstrate physical network serviceability.

facts.detail: If a rise was not specified or exceeds the contract term, the provider must give at least 30 days' notice.
The customer then has 30 days to exit or switch without an exit fee.

guard_streams.write_limit: A contractual switching right must not become a current-coverage candidate.

facts.detail: One Touch Switch launched for most customers on 12 September 2024.
Under One Touch Switch the gaining provider organises the broadband or landline switch, removing the need to cancel with the losing provider first.

guard_streams.write_limit: A successful switching process does not prove that a target parcel can receive a particular technology.

facts.detail: Ofcom concluded that most consumers switch successfully through OTS while provider matching issues required monitoring.
Ofcom states that use of a non-OTS alternative after repeated match failures stopped and industry compliance remains monitored.

guard_streams.write_limit: Switching-system matching records cannot populate postcode coverage, measured speed or parcel confidence.
